column1: # clues.tsv for ft_sqrt — pedagogic hints only. NEVER state the expected value or the fix.
# Format: <hint><TAB><member CASE label><TAB>...   (fires if ANY member case fails)
# Lines are shown most-fundamental first; the first line doubles as the "foothold".

This function returns a root only when the input is a perfect square. For a candidate r, what relationship between r and nb tells you r is THE answer? And when no such r exists, what single value stands for "no root"?
You searched and found no exact root. What does the return value have to be in that case, and is your loop deciding it correctly rather than handing back the nearest candidate?
Can a number below zero ever be a perfect square? What should you do before you even start searching?

As your candidate root grows, you square it to test it. For a large nb, how big does that product get, and does it still fit in the type you square it in? Pick a type wide enough that the comparison stays honest.
